segments: Tughril Beg sent an envoy to the Caliph al-Qaim, saying:
"I am a servant of the head of the kingdom of the Arabs,
and in all the regions over which I have ruled,
I have proclaimed the proclamation (khutba) of the Caliph,
and I have given rest to mankind from the oppression of the rulers Mahmud and Mas'ud, those who were before me.
And it is clear that I am not less than they.
They, indeed, were slaves of the Caliph and came to power;
whereas I am a freeman, of the lineage of the kingdom of the Huns (Turks).
And with these things,
if I am honored just as they were honored,
I hope that my submission and my gifts will be more than theirs."
It is said
that he, Tughril Beg, used to sit on a high throne,
and behind him were shields and spears,
and before him an excellent bow,
and in his hand two arrows,
and he would play with them.
And he used to wear white cotton clothes.
And on Monday and Thursday he used to fast,
and he would never neglect his five prayers at all.
And concerning his shrewdness, the chief judge (Qadi al-Qudat) of Baghdad relates:
"When I was sent as an envoy to him,
I wrote a secret letter to Baghdad,
and I made known in it his tyranny and his lack of mercy,
and that it was for show and not in the fear of the Lord that he prayed his prayers,
and other defects.
And I gave the letter to a man from my household,
and it fell from him,
and it was found and brought to him (Tughril Beg).
And when he understood everything that was in it,
he did not turn his face away from me at all,
nor did he diminish my honor.
And I did not perceive what had happened,
until on the way a certain scribe, a friend of mine, informed me,
and also the courier himself told me
that he had lost it on the road."
And when his troops came every day to pay homage to him, troop by troop,
each troop numbering two thousand,
from afar they would dismount from their horses {OCR? mounts},
and kiss the ground and stand.
Then one of those who were before him would make a sign to them
that their greeting had been accepted.
And again they would kiss the ground a second time, and mount, and depart,
and another troop would come.
And no man would approach him
or speak with him.
And wherever his troops gathered together,
they would take captives, lay waste, and kill.
And for more than a week
a region could not bear them because of their great number.
